english.title: Responsible person permits another to remove whole / part of a dog's tail
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the person responsible for a dog, permitted, or failed to take such steps as were reasonable in all the circumstances to prevent, another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), from removing the whole or part of that dog's tail otherwise than for the purpose of its medical treatment
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(2) and 32(1) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being the person responsible for a protected animal
permitted/failed to take such steps as were reasonable in all the circumstances
to prevent another person from carrying out a prohibited procedure on that animal
thereby causing it unnecessary suffering

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 6(3) of the Act provides that this offence does NOT APPLY if the dog is a certified working dog that is not more than 5 days old.
(ii) See section 6(4) to (7) for an explanation of the term "working dog", conditions and a defence.
(iii) See section 33 for privation orders.
(iv) See section 34 for disqualification from owning keeping animals.
(v) See section 35 for power to seize animals in connection with disqualification.
(vi) See section 37 for destruction in the interests of the animal.
(vii) See section 40 for the forfeiture of equipment used.
(viii) The maximum penalty for this offence was increased by the Animal Welfare (Sentencing) Act 2021 from the 29th April 2021, with the offence now becoming either way rather than summary. For the offence applying after 29th April 2021, see H22919 / AW06048.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant, being the person responsible for a dog, permitted, or failed to take such steps as were reasonable in all the circumstances to prevent, another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), from removing the whole or part of that dog's tail otherwise than for the purpose of its medical treatment.

other.timelimitforprosecutions: Complex see section 31 of the Act
other.penalty:
Summary: 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding £20,000.

NOTE:
Section 32(5) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides that In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months.

Complex see legislation
